model_ids.base_pipeline: black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell (gated on HF without a token; the identical files were taken from the ungated mirror unsloth/FLUX.1-schnell: CLIP-L text_encoder, T5-XXL text_encoder_2 in bf16, tokenizers, VAE, configs)

settings.negative_prompt: none (FLUX schnell takes no negative prompt; the prompts' 'No text, no frame...' clauses are the only exclusion)

first_attempt_832x1216.subject: octopus
first_attempt_832x1216.outcome: killed after 2 of 4 steps by the session's 30 min background-command limit (my error: no timeout set), not by memory; peak RAM through those steps stayed under the 15 GB machine

coverage: 1 of 6 images. Measured ~700 s per denoise step at 832x1216 on 4 CPU cores (~47 min per image); after the lost first attempt, only octopus s7001 fit the 90 min limit, run at 704x1024 (~520 s/step). biplane, canal and all 7002 seeds were not generated.
note:
Octopus s7001 (704x1024): a clean, convincing engraved plate with real cross hatching and good light from above, but only six arms; the 'beak' sketch reads as a bird's head, and the row of sucker details is missing. Prompt following on the negatives is poor: four corner labels and a full caption line of fake handwriting ('One test', 'The pile p ri le s liog...'), which oneink keeps as print, so they would need cropping or masking by hand.
In one ink it survives well (line mode, 7% coverage, no check fails); the suckers and the hatched arms hold up crisply. The cost is speed: ~500 s/step at 704x1024 and ~700 s/step at 832x1216 on this 4-core CPU (35-47 min per image), so only 1 of the 6 images exists. Not usable for batch work on this machine.
